test_title: PYST 3: SSC CGL Tier - II (English) (Held on: 29 Jan 2022)
subject: english
question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. “How do you manage to complete so much work?” he asked the student.

B. Looking at the huge pile of books on a student’s desk, a man said, “What a burden,my son! I pity you.”

C. “I focus on only one lesson at a time,” the student further added.

D. “I don’t think of all the work I have to do,” answered the student.
solution:
The correct answer is 'BADC'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some __grammatical or contextual__ connections between them. Also, the first sentence of a passage is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. 

__
 
• Sentence B is the independent sentence and points out the opening statement made by a person on seeing a huge number of books on a student's table. 
 
• So, sentence B is the first sentence after rearrangement. 
 
• Sentence A is a continuation of the the person's statement, where he asks the student a question regarding how they complete their work. Hence, A follows B.__
 
• Sentences **C **and **D **both are the answers given by the student. But sentence **C **ends with the phrase 'the student further added' which implies that it comes after another answer. 
 
• So, sentence **D **comes in the third position followed by sentence **C **as the concluding sentence. . 

Thus, the correct order after rearrangement is option 1 i.e. BADC.

So, the correct paragraph is : *(B)* ***Looking at the huge pile of books on a student’s desk, a man said, “What a burden,my son! I pity you.” (A) “How do you manage to complete so much work?” he asked the student.(D) “I don’t think of all the work I have to do,” answered the student. (C) “I focus on only one lesson at a time,” the student further added.***
